company: Red Hat, Inc. (OpenShift product line; subsidiary of IBM)

ownership.quote: IBM acquired all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Red Hat for $190.00 per share in cash, representing a total equity value of approximately $34 billion.

stage.quote: On October 28, 2018, IBM announced its intent to acquire Red Hat for $34 billion. The acquisition closed on July 9, 2019, and it now operates as an independent subsidiary of IBM.
stage.note: OpenShift is a product of Red Hat, which was a publicly traded, profitable company (NYSE: RHT) prior to being fully acquired by IBM in 2019; it now operates as a wholly owned IBM subsidiary rather than a VC-funded startup, so no funding-round stage applies.

total_funding_usd.basis: Full acquisition price paid by IBM to purchase all outstanding Red Hat shares (not a venture funding round, but the definitive change-of-control transaction value)
total_funding_usd.quote: IBM acquired all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Red Hat for $190.00 per share in cash, representing a total equity value of approximately $34 billion.

last_round.quote: IBM Closes Landmark Acquisition of Red Hat for $34 Billion; Defines Open, Hybrid Cloud Future

revenue.basis: IBM (parent company) total revenue per company financials, cited via Wikipedia infobox; Red Hat/OpenShift-specific revenue is not broken out separately by IBM

note: Red Hat OpenShift is a product of Red Hat, Inc., which has been a wholly owned subsidiary of IBM since the $34B acquisition closed in July 2019. Red Hat itself was previously an independent public company (NYSE: RHT) founded in 1993. No standalone revenue figure for OpenShift or Red Hat is disclosed by IBM post-acquisition; the revenue figure above is for IBM as a whole, per task guidance for subsidiaries of larger companies.
